title: Heteroskedastic load tiler and quantile-hypothesis export for cross-cohort regression analysis
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: existing benchmark runners model burstiness and multi-sequence mixes but do not adequately capture heteroskedastic behavior across modal subcohorts (e.g., chat vs. code vs. search) or provide a structured export suitable for hypothesis-driven quantile regression. This PR introduces two primary pieces: (1) a Heteroskedastic Load Tiler that deterministically slices and tiles incoming synthetic traffic into modal subcohorts with configurable variance profiles and warmup allocation rules, and (2) a Quantile-Hypothesis Exporter that produces per-run CSV/ndjson exports (and an optional proto payload) containing kernel-level and route-level quantile deltas suitable for automated regression scoring and downstream A/B analysis. Key goals: make cross-cohort comparisons reproducible, surface distributional shifts (not just mean/p95), and provide a compact export that can be consumed by the CI performance-bot and the regression analyzer pipeline.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Nice approach. Two asks before approving: add a deterministic-seed option in tiler config and a lightweight memory estimate for a worst-case tile size.
Author (Aisha): Added 'seed_replay' option and incorporated a O(1) heuristic for memory footprint in config.go comments; pushed a new test that asserts identical tiling with seed replay.
Tina Park: The quantile exporter format looks good. Can we make the kernel identifier stable across model swaps? Suggest canonicalizing to (model_name, model_hash, kernel_sig).
Author (Aisha): Exporter now includes model_hash and kernel_sig; updated schema comment and bumped ndjson schema version.

Sven Müller: CI bench matrix flaked on macOS runner due to pytest timing assert; recommend loosening timing tolerance for that environment or skipping. Also flagging a linter nit in tiler.go line 213.
Author (Aisha): Marked the macOS job as 'allow_failures' in the bench-export CI matrix and fixed linter nit. Added comment explaining why tolerance differs by platform.
ci_checks: bench-matrix: pass (linux amd64, linux arm64), macos marked allow_failures
artifact-upload: pass (quantile export attached as artifact)
perf_summary: Representative runs (stable seed replay) show expected widening of p50->p95 for hetero mixes: baseline single-modal p95 120ms -> hetero tiled p95 185ms (+54%). Per-kernel quantile export attached for downstream regression analysis. No CPU OOM observed in worst-case tiling during CI sample runs.
merge_outcome: merged via squash-merge. Merge commit message: 'feature(tiler,exporter): add heteroskedastic load tiler and quantile-hypothesis exporter for cross-cohort regression analysis (ENG-8721)'.
release_notes:
- Add Heteroskedastic Load Tiler to generate modal, seedable traffic tiles for benchmarks
- Add Quantile-Hypothesis Exporter (ndjson/csv) for per-kernel and route quantiles to support regression pipelines
- CI bench matrix job that uploads quantile artifacts for automated regression scoring
- Documentation and dashboard to visualize modal variance across runs
notes_for_maintainers: The tiler introduces a deterministic-seed mode; if you rely on fully random tiling remove the seed field or set seed_replay=false. The exporter schema is versioned; consumers should tolerate unknown fields.
